threads.body: `setUseXrayPropagator(false)` no longer fully disables X-Ray extraction: this argument enables the new `X-Amzn-Trace-Id` fallback whenever create spans are enabled. In the W3C-only configuration, a message whose configured propagation is absent or invalid can therefore be parented to an X-Ray context even though X-Ray propagation was explicitly disabled. Gate this fallback on `config.shouldUseXrayPropagator()` as well.

This process-context path has the same X-Ray-disable bypass as `SqsParentContext.ofMessage(message, config)`: the final argument controls extraction from the X-Ray message attribute, but it ignores `useXrayPropagator`. With the W3C-only test configuration, an X-Ray attribute can still become the process parent when configured propagation does not produce a span. Include `useXrayPropagator` in this condition.

[General] This gate also disables discovery of creation contexts that are already present. With the option off, such entries are no longer linked and the batch send remains `PRODUCER`; when configured message-attribute propagation is enabled, the legacy path can even overwrite an existing valid `traceparent` with the send span. The option is documented as disabling span creation only, so existing contexts should still be discovered/preserved; pass the flag into preparation to suppress only creation of missing contexts, and keep link/kind selection based on the discovered contexts.

Analysis: The create-span flag guarded context preparation and the link and span-kind logic. The stable semantic-convention path now always discovers existing contexts. The flag only skips creating and injecting contexts for entries that lack one. Stable batch sends also bypass the legacy send-span propagation path, so existing message attributes remain unchanged.

Upsides: Existing per-message contexts remain linked, batch sends use CLIENT kind when links exist, and valid traceparent values are preserved when create spans are disabled. Focused tests cover both AWS SDK generations.

Downsides: Stable batch sends with create spans disabled still inspect each entry for an existing context. No material compatibility downside identified.

Analysis: The builder documentation described user message-attribute capacity as a universal requirement. AWS SDK v1 uses the AWSTraceHeader system attribute. AWS SDK v2 can use either that system attribute or the configured messaging propagator. The revised text states the eligibility rule for each SDK generation and limits the capacity requirement to the carrier that uses message attributes.

Upsides: Users can tell when create spans are available and understand that system attributes do not consume the ten user message-attribute slots.

Downsides: The AWS SDK v2 description is longer because it covers both propagation carriers. No material downside identified.

threads.body: [General] This stable-semconv return also disables the previous batch injection through the configured messaging propagator. In a W3C-only setup (`useXrayPropagator=false`), disabling create spans leaves entries without an existing context completely unpropagated: the send span remains `PRODUCER`, but receivers cannot parent or link to it. Please fall back to injecting the send span into context-free entries when no per-message creation contexts are used, while still preserving valid contexts already present.

replies.body:
Addressed in d2cec32457a9df06895414ed6738b43c443000d9.

Analysis: Stable batch preparation still records valid W3C and X-Ray contexts when create spans are disabled. The later propagation step now injects the send span only into entries that have no valid creation context. It leaves valid message-attribute and system-attribute contexts untouched. The existing legacy behavior remains unchanged outside stable messaging semantic conventions.

Upsides: Context-free entries retain send-span propagation in W3C-only setups, while entries with custom contexts keep their original values and links. The regression test covers both cases in one batch.

Downsides: The fallback extracts each entry context again before deciding whether to inject the send span. No material compatibility downside identified.

X-Ray enablement gates both that request header and the per-entry `AWSTraceHeader`. threads.body: With a no-op tracer, `Instrumenter.start()` returns an invalid span context. Default X-Ray propagation then produces no header, but `injectCreationContext()` still adds an `AWSTraceHeader` with a null string value and treats injection as successful, which can make an otherwise valid batch request fail validation. End the attempted span and skip injection when the returned context is invalid.

replies.body:
Addressed in 43cc263546e187c0eef0082b3950c76644d128d3.

Analysis: Both SDK versions assumed that a started create instrumenter always returned a valid span context. A no-op OpenTelemetry instance returns an invalid context, so X-Ray injection cannot produce a trace header. Both paths now end the attempted span and leave the batch entry unchanged instead of injecting a null system attribute.

Upsides: No-op telemetry can send SQS batches without invalid message system attributes. Regression tests cover the behavior in both SDK versions.

Downsides: Each eligible batch entry now performs one span-context validity check.
